messages:
Sam: heads-up — customer reported a BYOK HSM import that shows as 'success' in their console but our audit stream has no wrap/unwrap events for that import id: imp_3f9a. Can someone sanity-check?
Anya: which pipeline did they use to import? sidecar proxy or direct-cloud-hsm?
Sam: they used our hsm-proxy (v2) via the onboarding flow. import id and tenant id attached in the ticket.
Devon: quick note — we rolled an RBAC tweak last Thursday that tightened operator -> wrapKey permission. iirc that change also touched the proxy's audit level (PR 3246). possible suppression?
Priya: running a grep across recent logs, try: 
```
kubectl -n hsm-proxy logs -l app=hsm-proxy --since=48h | grep imp_3f9a || true
```
Priya: also check sidecar stdout for `wrapKey` / `ExportWrappedKey` traces, sometimes they live in a different container (proxy vs importer).
Marta: SecBot flagged an INFO-level event for a key creation around that time but no corresponding 'import-complete' audit entry in the central audit index. link: https://ci.example/alerts/8921 :thinking_face:
SecBot: automated alert — HSM import observed (imp_3f9a) from tenant:tenant-42, severity: info, components: hsm-proxy, importer-sidecar.
Anya: if RBAC change degraded audit to INFO/WARN only, compliance needs an unequivocal RECORD of wrap/unwrapped ops (for SOC2). We must assume missing logs = missing evidence until proven otherwise.
Devon: triage plan suggestion: 1) reproduce import on staging with same proxy version, 2) enable debug audit flag in staging, 3) run grep across archived audit index for imp_3f9a and related correlation id, 4) check kube-audit for suppressed events.
Sam: agree. can someone own steps 1+2? I'll open an incident and ping legal/compliance after we have reproduction notes.
Priya: i'll spin a staging job and flip `AUDIT_LEVEL=debug` on the proxy, then re-import a sanitized test key. i'll post logs here. ETA 2h.
Marta: i'll run a search in the log-warehouse for wrap/unwrapped keywords and for any rewrap events tied to tenant-42. run: `es query wrapKey AND tenant-42` but will also check hot-indexes.
Devon: FYI also check KMS integration path — if the importer did a double-hop (customer HSM -> our proxy -> external KMS) our central audit pipeline may have dropped low-severity proxy messages before canonicalization. that mapping lives in infractl routing rules.
Sam: action items: Priya (repro + debug logs), Marta (warehouse search + export), Devon (audit pipeline mapping + RBAC diff), Anya (coordinate compliance notification draft). I created incident INC-2026-59: https://tracker.example/INC-2026-59 — assign folks there.
Priya: quick repro log snippet (staging) — proxy received import, then importer returned 200, but central-audit pipeline shows an ingestion latency spike and then a retry that ended in a 400 for `canonicalize_event`:
```
[hsm-proxy] 2026-03-21T14:05:12Z INFO Received import imp_test123
[importer] 2026-03-21T14:05:12Z INFO import success id=imp_test123
[audit-sink] 2026-03-21T14:05:13Z WARN ingestion latency ms=3120
[audit-sink] 2026-03-21T14:05:13Z ERROR canonicalize_event failed status=400 error=missing_field:wrap_info
```
Marta: that `missing_field:wrap_info` smells like a canonicalizer schema change. maybe RBAC change removed the field or proxy started emitting a different field name. i'll diff the canonicalizer schema against last-deployed.
Devon: good catch — if schema mismatch is why we dropped events, remediation is twofold: patch canonicalizer to accept both names (hotfix) + backfill missing wrap_info by replaying raw proxy logs into a temporary canonicalizer. backfill may be required for audit evidence.
Sam: compliance note — if we need a backfill, legal wants a signed affidavit of the scope and timing. Anya, can you prepare a compliance timeline template while we confirm technical fix?
Anya: on it. i'll draft a short timeline and checklist for evidence (raw logs, staging repro, canonicalizer changes, RBAC PR diff). will post by EOD.
Sam: thanks all. please update INC-2026-59 with findings. keep channel updated for any P0 escalation. :thumbsup:
